pages.text: Learn to Earn: The Long-Term Effects of Foundational Learning | NBER Skip to main content Learn to Earn: The Long-Term Effects of Foundational Learning Tahir Andrabi , Natalie Bau , Jishnu Das , Asim Ijaz Khwaja & Catherine Michaud-Leclerc Share X LinkedIn Facebook Bluesky Threads Email Link Working Paper 36030 DOI 10.3386/w36030 Issue Date November 2026 Tracking Pakistani students over 15 years, we use two identification strategies to provide the first causal evidence linking learning in primary school to adult outcomes in a low-income country. Exposure to a school with higher test score value-added increases educational attainment and earnings 15 years later. A randomized information intervention that led to learning gains at the village level generated similar effects. Lifetime earnings gains across all students attending a 1sd better school total US$175,000, and for the information intervention, the marginal value of public funds is infinity for men. There is a strong economic case for investing in learning. Cecilia Peterson December 9, 2021 Get our Newsletter! Get our Newsletter! My grandpa Harold, uncle Curt, cousin Eric, grandma Lucille, and cousin Nils at Christmas in the early 1980s. Photo courtesy of Cecilia Peterson When my friend Kat returned from a vacation in Sweden this year, she told me, “Hey, did you know that no one knows what potatis korv is there? People were confused whenever I asked about it.” Now, I don’t believe most people speak so casually about obscure sausage varieties, but Kat happens to have made potatis korv with me for years, in preparation for my annual Christmas smörgåsbord . I’ve never been to Sweden myself, despite exactly half of my ancestors claiming Swedish heritage. Still, it surprised me—I can’t remember a year in my life where my Grandma Lucille laid out the smörgåsbord and the korv was missing. But apparently, potatis korv is a regional dish, though Swedish Americans all over the United States may know exactly what it is. pages.text: Leave Benefits | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Leave Benefits More in This Section Close Family and Medical Leave (FMLA) Funeral Leave Government Contracts Holidays Jury Duty Personal Leave Sick Leave Vacations Many companies offer leave benefits that allow employees to take time off from work for various reasons. Leave benefits – whether paid, unpaid or partially paid – are generally an agreement between the employer and employee, or employees representative (such as a union). Family and Medical Leave Act The Family and Medical Leave Act provides certain employees with up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave per year. It also requires that their group health benefits be maintained during the leave. Fair Labor Standards Act While certain types of leave are required by law, other types are voluntary incentives provided by employers. There is a common misconception that Department of Labor regulates leave benefits through the Fair Labor Standards Act . But, the FLSA only covers certain types of leave. In fact, there are a number of employment practices which FLSA does not regulate. For example, it does not require: Vacation, holiday, severance, or sick pay Meal or rest periods, holidays off, or vacations Premium pay for weekend or holiday work Pay raises or fringe benefits Discharge notice, reason for discharge, or immediate payment of final wages to terminated employees Statistics The Employee Benefits Survey of the Bureau of Labor Statistics covers the incidence and characteristics of employee benefits.

Social Media Census Bureau Blog(s), X (Twitter), Facebook, YouTube and other social media channels allow visitors to interact with the agency and others, and encourage visitors to freely comment and give welcomed feedback. pages.description: Scientists need postmortem human brains for research, but general organ donation programs don’t harvest them. Tish Hevel found a solution.
pages.text: Leaving your brain to science: don’t let myths dissuade you | National Geographic This donated brain of a 101-year-old man is larger than a typical brain of someone his age. He’s said to have been astute until the day he died. Photograph By Rebecca Hale Premium MAGAZINE Leaving your brain to science: don’t let myths dissuade you Scientists need postmortem human brains for research, but general organ donation programs don’t harvest them. Tish Hevel found a solution. By Lori Cuthbert 3 min read This story appears in the October 2018 issue of National Geographic magazine. Brains are in short supply. Neuroscientists need brain tissue of all types to study the diseases that affect more than 15 percent of people in the world. Enter Tish Hevel. In 2015, after Hevel’s father died from Lewy body dementia, her family wanted to offer his brain for research—but knew that it would take much more than an organ donor card. The experience inspired Hevel to create the Brain Donor Project “to raise awareness of the critical need” and make enrolling easier for would-be donors. Nearly two years in, more than 2,000 people have signed up. 3:43 Busting myths about donating your brain The organization that Tish Hevel created—online at braindonorproject.org —aims to simplify “the process of donating postmortem human brains for research,” she says, and dispel misconceptions about it. Legal Authorities for Isolation and Quarantine For Everyone May 15, 2024 At a glance Federal regulations allow staff at U.S. Port Health Stations to take certain actions to limit the introduction and spread of communicable diseases in the United States. These stations, located at major U.S. ports of entry, serve as focal points for responses to infections in travelers that could lead to outbreaks in destination communities. Isolation and Quarantine Isolation and quarantine help protect the public by preventing exposure to people who have or may have a contagious disease. Isolation separates sick people with a quarantinable communicable disease from people who are not sick. Quarantine separates and restricts the movement of people who were exposed to a contagious disease to see if they become sick. In addition to serving as health functions, isolation and quarantine also are "police power" functions, derived from the right of the state to take action affecting individuals for the benefit of society. In 1553-4 he visited Venice and Rome, and after 1559 he was in Novellara. There are no contemporary records of his paintings, and no signed works, except one drawing. A group of small religious paintings, all by the same hand, are attributed to him. They show the influence of Michelangelo and Correggio . The inscription on his grave at Novellara (written by his son) says that he was great in architecture and painting, but greatest as a draughtsman. Some of the drawings attributed to him bear this out. pages.text: Lelio Orsi | The Walk to Emmaus | NG1466 | National Gallery, London Skip to main content Lelio Orsi, 'The Walk to Emmaus', about 1565-75 The Walk to Emmaus Lelio Orsi Room 6 About the work Overview In-depth Overview The Gospel of Luke tells how after the Crucifixion, Cleopas and another of Christ’s disciples set out from Jerusalem for the village of Emmaus. They were joined by a stranger who recounted the prophecies concerning the Messiah’s death and resurrection. It was not until the three ate together later at an inn in Emmaus that the disciples recognised the risen Christ (Luke 24: 13–29). Lelio Orsi sets the episode on an overcast evening – bursts of light break through black clouds, casting a supernatural glow. One disciple clasps his belt while the other wrings his hands in anguish as Christ in the centre explains the prophecies. The small goldfinch in the bottom right-hand corner is a common symbol of the Passion (Christ’s torture and crucifixion). The painting, which probably dates to about 1565–75, reveals Orsi’s interest in the work of Michelangelo, which he would have seen on an earlier trip to Rome. pages.text: Leonardo's horse took 500 years to make | National Geographic Published April 30, 2019 • 2 min read Studies of horses drawn by Leonardo da Vinci circa 1490, when he was planning “Il Gran Cavallo.” Collection of the Royal Library, Windsor Castle, Windsor, England Photograph by Print Collector/Album At the request of Ludovico Sforza, the future Duke of Milan , Leonardo da Vinci began working on a sculpture that would be the largest equestrian statue in the world in 1482. Leonardo made sketches of the horses in the Sforza stables, from which he designed a 24-foot-high clay model. Leonardo wanted to cast the horse in a single operation and designed elaborate plaster molds to make that possible. In his innovative process, the inverted molds would be buried between two ovens, and molten bronze would fill them to cast the statue. War versus art The plans were set to create the giant horse, but war with France engulfed Milan in 1499. Sforza needed the bronze for weapons, not art, and the materials were diverted to forge cannons. The French defeated Milan, occupied Sforza's lands, and destroyed the clay horse. Leonardo ’s drawings and plans survived, but the artist died in May 1519 before “Il Gran Cavallo” could be brought to life. Dent made it his life’s work to erect the statue. pages.text: Lessons of the Hour | Perth Museum Explore Isaac Julien's acclaimed film portrait of Frederick Douglass at Perth Museum Perth Museum is the first and only Scottish venue on this new ARTIST ROOMS tour of Isaac Julien’s (b.1960) immersive film installation Lessons of the Hour - Frederick Douglass 2019 . This exhibition brings Julien’s poetic meditation on the life and legacy of Frederick Douglass into dialogue with the histories of abolition, slavery and racial justice in Perthshire and across Scotland. Born into slavery in Maryland in 1818, Douglass became a pioneering abolitionist, writer and intellectual, playing a critical role in anti-slavery and human rights movements in the US, Britain and beyond. During his 1846 campaign against slavery across the UK and Ireland, Douglass delivered four speeches in Perth in the former City Hall building, on the very site where Perth Museum now stands. Julien’s work, and in turn this exhibition, takes its title from Douglass’ final delivered speech in 1894. Photo by Joe Furgal, Ralph Rinzler Folklife Archives A common idiom in American English casts the circus in an unfavorable light: “It’s a circus over there!” tends to mean something messy and chaotic. Yet if you look at the inner workings of an actual circus, the level of skill, coordination, and execution necessary for such a production is immeasurable. The split-second timing of a flying trapeze catch, the unspoken understanding and total trust between acrobats as they tower atop each other, the quick-wittedness of a clown as they turn an unscripted interaction into a highlight of the show—these performances require lifetimes of training, the strictest schedules, and the perfectly coordinated efforts of teams both in the spotlight and in the wings. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail In 1803, Meriwether Lewis and William Clark embarked on their historic expedition along what we now recognize as the Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail. Stretching roughly 4,900 miles from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, to Astoria, Oregon, this trail traverses 16 states and numerous tribal lands, preserving a crucial chapter in American history. Managed by various federal land management agencies, as well as state, local, tribal, and private organizations, sections of the trail provide visitors with an authentic glimpse into the landscapes encountered by the explorers. Notably, the 2019 John D. Dingell, Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act expanded the trail by an additional 1,200 miles along the Ohio and Mississippi Rivers, linking Pittsburgh to Wood River, Illinois. One prominent landmark along the route is Pompey’s Pillar National Monument in Montana, where Captain Clark's signature remains engraved—a tangible link to the expedition's passage. "We're constantly working on our communication," said Hamilton, who had a different race engineer last year. "It's been a lot better this year. Carlos (sic) has done an amazing job. pages.text: Lexi Kilfoyl's dominant relief appearance sends Bandits to AUSL Championship Series Skip to Content In a thrilling 11-inning play-in victory over the Portland Cascade on Thursday night to punch their ticket to the AUSL Championship Series against the Utah Talons, the Chicago Bandits got a tremendous performance by right-hander Lexi Kilfoyl. Kilfoyl came on in relief of starter Kat Sandercock in the fifth inning with her team trailing, 3-0. And from there, Kilfoyl was nearly unhittable over seven innings. With the length of a regulation game being seven innings in softball, her appearance was as long as a complete game. Kilfoyl faced 28 batters and yielded just two hits while walking none, hitting a batter and striking out four on an incredible 115 pitches. ATHLETES UNLIMITED SOFTBALL LEAGUE Talons win second straight AUSL title Everything to know about AUSL All-Star Cup Complete AUSL coverage Although Portland scratched across a pair of runs against Kilfoyl, both were unearned. And she did not allow a hit over her final five innings -- Cascade batters were 0-for-23 during that stretch. The clutch performance was reminiscent of some of the greatest -- and longest -- relief appearances in MLB history. And by number of innings and pitches, it would be a rare feat in the Major Leagues. Since 1994, there has only been one instance in the Majors of a relief pitcher going at least seven innings and throwing at least 115 pitches. That was Jordan Lyles for the Rangers against the A’s on Sept. 11, 2020, when he went seven innings and threw exactly 115 pitches.

Hier soir, j’ai présenté dans l’amphithéâtre C002 au sein du campus de enseeiht à Toulouse, « Contribuez à OSM ». La bonne surprise fut le taux de remplissage de la salle. J’ai compté plus d’une vingtaine de personnes. La présentation était articulée en deux parties : la première, un tout petit peu de théorie et pas de présentation d’outils ; la deuxième, des démonstrations, des petits trucs faciles pour commencer, puis des trucs plus « grands » (de l’infrastructure). En trente minutes, j’avais plié ma présentation. Il restait vingt-cinq minutes, qui se sont très, très facilement remplies par de très nombreuses questions. Merci au plublic pour ces questions. pages.text: Liam Hendriks 2023 American League Comeback Player of the Year Skip to Content CHICAGO -- Liam Hendriks didn’t return from a subpar previous season or an injury to be named the 2023 American League Comeback Player of the Year. No, this particular award represents more of a real-life feel, after Hendriks battled Stage 4 non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma. Hendriks announced his condition on Jan. 8 , and it reached remission on April 20 . The right-hander made his season debut on May 29 at Guaranteed Rate Field, in what was arguably the top moment of the 2023 season for the White Sox. But it would have been the club's top moment even if it had won 101 games instead of losing 101. Simply put, Hendriks was and is an inspiration . “Oh my God. That was the most important thing ever. That was beyond baseball. This is life-threatening. This is not a [Tommy John],” White Sox manager Pedro Grifol said of Hendriks during an end-of-season interview. “You are talking about battling cancer. “This is real, and who cares about baseball. This is one of the good guys in the game. He cares about others, he’s selfless and is always serving. I just wanted him to put a uniform back on. When he did that, it was a really emotional thing for us.” The 34-year-old Hendriks -- who was joined in this award by National League recipient Cody Bellinger -- received support from fans, teammates, members of the White Sox organization, players from outside the White Sox and from the few Major League players who had dealt with the same insidious illness. En muchos casos estas organizaciones han desempeñado un papel importante en la transformación democrática de sus países. La OIT está comprometida a promover la libertad sindical en sus actividades, por ejemplo a través de la asesoría a gobiernos sobre legislación laboral, o la formación y capacitación dirigida hacia sindicatos o grupos empleadores. El Comité de libertad sindical de la OIT fue creado en 1951 para examinar los alegatos sobre violaciones a los derechos de organización de trabajadores y empleadores. El Comité es tripartita y maneja casos de todos los Estados miembros de la OIT, aunque no hayan ratificado los Convenios sobre este tema. A través del Comité de libertad sindical y de otros órganos de supervisión la OIT ha defendido con frecuencia los derechos de organizaciones de trabajadores y empleadores. Library and information science is a field of study that encompasses all of the aspects of the creation, organization, documentation, management, communication, and use of recorded information. It is the umbrella term for a wide variety of fields of study and work, including librarianship, information management, knowledge management, archiving, and records management, and is tangential to museum studies. While library science and information science are two separate disciplines, they are interrelated and are often used synonymously. The Zawiya refinery, west of the capital Tripoli, was hit in a drone strike on Monday evening - the third such incident in two days. The National Oil Corporation (NOC) said a tank containing about 4.5m litres of fuel was directly hit, triggering a huge fire that caused it to collapse. It said it was considering suspending operations if the attacks continued. There were no "serious injuries" from the fire, with most patients treated for smoke inhalation, Libya's Ambulance and Emergency Service said on Tuesday. The Zawiya refinery is the largest operational facility in Libya, with an output of 120,000 barrels per day. The NOC condemned similar attacks in past days in Zawiya, including two drone strikes on a naphtha reservoir and a water desalination plant. It called on the authorities to investigate who was behind the violence. The attacks have highlighted continuing instability in Libya, which has been split in two since a civil war broke out after the ousting of former leader Muammar Gaddafi. Life Cycle Greenhouse Gas Perspective on Exporting Liquefied Natural Gas from the United States On May 29, 2014, the Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Fossil Energy announced the availability for public review and comment the report Life Cycle Greenhouse Gas Perspective on Exporting Liquefied Natural Gas from the United States (LCA GHG Report). The purpose of this LCA GHG Report is to provide additional information to the public and to DOE to inform its decisions regarding the life cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions of U.S. LNG exports for use in electric power generation. The LCA GHG Report compares life cycle GHG emissions from U.S. LNG exports to regional coal and other imported natural gas for electric power generation in Europe and Asia. The LCA GHG Report is based on the NETL report Life Cycle Analysis of Natural Gas Extraction and Power Generation (Natural Gas and Power LCA Model Documentation).
